I’d like the option to turn on photorealistic shading, texture, and coloration that looks more like the cadavers do in the cadaver lab. Arteries and nerves the same color (more or less), veins blueish/black, etc. Basically I wish you could hit a button and turn it from “beautifully illustrated anatomy textbook” to look more like the Mark Nielsen/Shawn Miller cadaver photos lecture that they have available for purchase. In an ideal world, they’d make the muscles floppy, flaccid, or even give the option to show what the muscle looks like when atrophied (like they often are with elderly donors in the lab), but this would be a pretty deep rewrite of the 3D models, compared to the more “doable” updating of the model textures. Last gripe: I wish you could temporarily disable bones and muscles from being selected (while still having them visible for reference). I don’t have particularly fat fingers, but if I’m studying nerves, it’s almost impossible to select a nerve without zooming in 1000% just to make sure you’re don’t select the bone/muscles nearby instead.

title: I’ve had this app for several years now
body: I’m 35(F) and initially, I had downloaded this app a few years ago to help me better understand a cancer diagnosis and some of the procedures I’d undergo for treatment. I’m a bit of a control freak, so the only thing that could possibly relieve my anxiety was researching and seeing what body parts were impacted and how certain issues can cause a chain reaction with other organs. I have to say, this app did more for my mental health than any of my doctors (who were amazing, btw). Understanding how these organs work, and how to take care of my body through these procedures, allowed me to feel more in control of my health and recovery. Thankfully, I’ve been cleared of any signs of cancer for 2 years now, but I continue to pay for this app because I use it for everything! More recently, I was playing a fire 🔥 game of pickleball (don’t hate) and twisted my ankle pretty aggressively. I tried to continue to play on it, but pretty soon my whole leg when numb and I collapsed. I still didn’t want to go to Urgent Care, but a few hours later I cracked open this app and inspected the tendons where my injury occurred (and blood was pooling). Thanks to C. Anatomy, I realized pretty quickly that my injury was a bit more serious than I thought, so I went to Urgent Care. While at UC, the radiologist showed me that I had a grade 3 eversion ankle sprain affecting the exact tendons (and nerves, which caused the numbness in my leg) that C. Anatomy had indicated. I showed the radiologist this app, halfway expecting him to scoff at me for playing “Dr. Google” but he didn’t — he said that he’s recommended it to patients in the past for help with understanding injuries and ailments. C. Anatomy is 100% worth the money. Better than therapy for people who suffer from anxiety from lack of information. The movement videos, stretches, and layer options simply cannot be beat. There is nothing like this app. Thank you so much to the developers. Without you guys, I may not have made a full recovery — mental health plays such a role in beating cancer and seeking treatment, and this app really did save me. 🤍

title: So very good but also very annoying
body: I’ve looked far and wide for an excellent app to study brain anatomy. Primarily I want to learn the spatial relationships between the different structures of the brain. This app is what I’ve been looking for and, bonus, it includes the rest of the body. The thing that is most annoying, and I hope it gets fixed soon, is that the view resets itself often. By the view, I mean you can focus on particular parts and hide others. For me, I want the brain, and only the brain showing. And I’ll hide parts of the brain to ease my studies. It takes careful work to get to this point. I have to choose to show the nervous system, and hide other body systems. Depending on the complexity of the view you want, it can take 5-10 minutes or more to set it up. What I’d love at this point is to be able to save the view. And then come back to it. Instead, even with background app refresh on, if you switch to another app, let your screen turn off, etc., the app will reset the view to the default view, which is the skeletal system. So close to being so good, yet so far.
